I had this idea for Reddit, but you know...

So instead of registering a new account when you want a throwaway, why not let us create an alias from within our account, that we can then delete once we are done with. The alias would ofc have no link back to the main profile, short of having easy access to post as it.

Thoughts?

The problem with this is that your main account will still be tied to your throwaway one on the server side (e.g. at least in the logs). If there's a data leak (and we've learned in the past years that this can always happen no matter what), then it all pours out.

So I'd rather spend an extra minute or two to create a real throwaway and be safe. (incognito window, geo proxy etc) and keep calm.
Plus, I can see throwaway accounts being abused by the more unsavoury users.
What if there was an option to post as "anonymous"? Everything would simply be stored on the anonymous account, with no ties to the main account.

Aye, but then everyone is anonymous, and subsequent replies are not verifiable as coming from OP... Unless this is somehow addressed.

Caveat - Not a programmer.
I like the idea of having the option to be able to reply or post a thread as anonymous and not getting up/down CCP from it. However, the posts would still follow the same CCP rules.
I do believe this idea was suggested yesterday.

How about a built-in throwaway-style account. It could expire after a defined period of time, maybe a day or an hour or a year. When creating an account you could choose whether to make it a regular account or a throwaway... and how long you wanted it for. Also, it would have no voting privileges -- or voting privileges only within its own submissions.
